inline_comments.comment: `[data-look=neo].labelBkg` is a combined-attribute-and-class selector: it matches a single element that simultaneously has the `data-look="neo"` attribute AND the `labelBkg` class. But `data-look` is set on node group elements (e.g. the `<g class="node default">` wrapper), while `.labelBkg` lives on edge-label background elements — these are never the same DOM node. The rule is therefore dead and will never apply. It should be a descendant selector: `[data-look=neo] .labelBkg` (with a space).

`genColor` early-returns for any theme other than `'redux-color'`, so it never emits CSS rules for `'redux-dark-color'`. However, in `erBox.ts`, `COLOR_THEMES = new Set(['redux-color', 'redux-dark-color'])` and `data-color-id` is stamped onto node elements for both themes. The result is that `'redux-dark-color'` nodes receive the `data-color-id` attribute but have no matching CSS rules to colour them — the color-indexing feature is silently broken for the dark variant. Either extend `genColor` to handle both color themes, or align `COLOR_THEMES` with what `genColor` actually supports.

The `data-color-id` attribute block (the three-line `if (theme != null && COLOR_THEMES.has(theme))` guard) appears twice: once in the early-return path for attributeless entities (~line 66) and again here in the main rendering path. The duplication means any future change to this logic must be made in two places. Consider extracting it into a small helper such as `applyColorId(shapeSvg, entityNode, theme, borderColorArray)` and calling it from both paths.

The new `-pointEnd-margin`, `-pointStart-margin`, `-circleEnd-margin`, `-circleStart-margin`, `-crossEnd-margin`, and `-crossStart-margin` marker definitions are appended inside the generic `point()`, `circle()`, and `cross()` builder functions. These functions are called for every diagram type that uses these marker shapes — flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, etc. — so every such diagram now gets these extra `<marker>` elements defined in its SVG `<defs>`, even if they are never referenced. If these margin markers are only consumed by ER neo-look edges, they should be defined in a dedicated ER-marker function (or in the neo marker functions) rather than injected into the generic builders.

Each of the four neo marker functions (`only_one_neo`, `zero_or_one_neo`, `one_or_more_neo`, `zero_or_more_neo`) independently calls `configApi.getConfig()` and destructures `themeVariables`. This creates four separate config lookups per diagram render. The classic marker functions accept all required values through their parameters. Consider either passing `strokeWidth` (and `mainBkg` where needed) as a fourth parameter — keeping parity with the classic API — or computing them once in the caller (`insertMarkers`) and forwarding them.

There is a double space in the CSS selector on this line: `[data-look="${look}"][data-color-id="color-${i}"].node  rect`. Two consecutive spaces between `.node` and `rect` don't change the selector's meaning (whitespace in descendant combinators is collapsed), but it is inconsistent with the single-space used in the `.node path` rule directly above.

`looks` is declared as a one-element tuple and only used to drive a `forEach`. Using an array + `forEach` for a single value adds indirection without benefit. If additional looks are genuinely expected to be added later, that intent is worth a comment; otherwise a simple `const look = 'neo' as const` (and removing the outer `forEach`) would make the intent clearer.

general_comments.comment: The `DiagramStylesProvider` type used for both `genColor` and `getStyles` is defined as `(options?: any) => string`, which erases all static type information for the options bag. The original `FlowChartStyleOptions` was a concrete interface. As new properties like `look`, `theme`, `erEdgeLabelBackground`, `strokeWidth`, `bkgColorArray`, and `borderColorArray` are accessed on `options`, none of them are checked by the compiler. Consider defining a dedicated `ErStyleOptions` interface (extending or composing with the existing theme-variable types) so that typos and missing properties are caught at compile time rather than silently producing `undefined` at runtime.
